Subject: DPA redlines - Acme Health / Redwood

Olga,

Thanks for the quick turn. Please see our attached redlines to the DPA (v3) and a separate spreadsheet with our required subprocessors disclosure. High-level asks:
- We need the full list of subprocessors (new requirement for our procurement team) and a comms plan for future additions.
- Confirm the EU/UK transfer mechanism. Our counsel expects a UK Addendum + SCCs or an equivalent binding mechanism.
- We cannot accept blanket subprocessor delegation clauses without a written notice and opt-out window.

Can you confirm you can accept the redlines or highlight any non-starters by EOD Thurs? We have an internal June 1st go-live and procurement is slowing us down.

Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines - Acme Health / Redwood

Julia —

Thanks for sharing. A quick read: most redlines are standard procurement asks. Two items I want to flag immediately and loop legal on:
1) UK Addendum + SCCs: we can provide SCCs but our standard practice is to pair SCCs with our internal transfer assessments. We don’t currently have a separate "UK Addendum" as a standalone doc — legal, can you confirm if we will sign a UK Addendum for this account?
2) Subprocessor notification: we have an automated 30-day advance notice process for new subprocessors; redline removes materiality/notice windows. That will need an exception approval if Acme requires a notice plus opt-out period.

Karthik/Marissa — see attached redlines from Acme. Can legal confirm the exposure and whether exec-level exception approval will be required? Goal: close contractual terms this week or early next week to hit Acme's June timeline.

Thanks,
Olga
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines - Acme Health / Redwood

Team —

Reviewed Acme's attached redlines. Summary of non-starters and risk:
- UK Addendum: we don't have a generic UK Addendum productized, but we can sign the EU SCCs + a short schedule that mirrors our transfer practices. Acme's proposed language is broader than our standard and would create operational obligations we cannot commit to without product change (e.g., on-prem key escrow).
- Subprocessor opt-out window: Acme wants a 30-day opt-out that allows them to terminate if a new subprocessor is unacceptable. Our standard is 30-day notice + ability to object and we’ll offer to provide a migration plan if they're uncomfortable. Committing to termination for new subprocessors is a high operational risk.
- Liability/indemnity tweaks in Section 6: within reason but need limits tightened.

If Acme insists on their current phrasing, we will need exec risk sign-off (legal + GTM leadership) because it changes our product commitments. If they can accept SCCs + narrow UK schedule + our notice+object flow for subprocessors, we can proceed fast.

Requesting: Rishi, can you approve an expedited exception to allow a one-off UK schedule and to accept notice+object (not opt-out) for this deal up to $X ARR? If approval requires escalation beyond your level, please advise who to route to.

Karthik
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference

From: contracts@acmehealth.com <contracts@acmehealth.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines - Acme Health / Redwood

Olga/Karthik —

Appreciate the quick review. A few clarifications from Acme counsel:
- SCCs alone are insufficient for our legal team. They require a named UK Addendum referencing UK ICO expectations (we will share a template).
- The notice+object flow is acceptable only if we have a guaranteed migration commitment in the contract in the event of a critical subprocessor that jeopardizes data security.
- We also need a DocuSign packet for the final DPA; please provide a signed copy route so our procurement can track execution.

Can you provide: the full current subprocessor list with regions, your proposed SCC + schedule draft, and a DocuSign packet by COB Fri 17 Apr? If not, procurement will need to push this internally which will delay the June milestone.

Regards,
Acme Health Legal

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 16 Apr 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Escalation: Acme DPA asks - need exception sign-off and timeline decision

Folks —

Acme is pushing for a UK Addendum + a stronger migration obligation tied to subprocessor objections. They want the packet and DocuSign by COB Fri (tomorrow). From a product/legal perspective the migration commitment as written is risky (open-ended termination/migration costs). Karthik, I agree with your recommendation: offer SCCs + a narrow UK schedule that reflects our internal processes, and provide a subprocessor migration SLA limited to reasonable efforts and transition support.

Rishi — this is a high-probability close (pilot -> enterprise) and timeboxed (June 1). We need an exception approval to agree to a one-off UK schedule and to finalize DocuSign routing. Approve the exception for this account (up to $X ARR exposure) or tell us who to escalate to so we can meet Acme's timeline.

If we don't respond by tomorrow with a signed packet they will push procurement and delay on their side. I'm concerned about losing momentum.

Thanks,
Olga

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 16 Apr 2026 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Escalation: Acme DPA asks - need exception sign-off and timeline decision

Olga —

Approve a limited exception: we can accept a one-off UK schedule that mirrors SCCs and agree to notice+object workflow. Do NOT accept open-ended migration termination liability. Karthik — please draft the UK schedule and limited migration language consistent with that guidance and loop in me if any downstream financial exposure exceeds the deal threshold.

Rishi
VP, Sales Operations

Subject: Re: Contract clearance - DPA redlines & UK Addendum (Acme Health)

Julia —

Thanks for the patience. Per my internal escalation: we can do the following to keep your timeline intact:
1) We will sign SCCs + a one-off UK schedule that reflects Redwood's transfer assessments (attached draft).
2) For subprocessors: we will provide the current list (attached) and agree to a 30-day advance notice + objection process. If objection triggers a critical security concern, we will provide a defined migration plan and reasonable transition support — not an automatic termination right.
3) Karthik will prepare the final DPA + UK schedule; I will route a DocuSign packet for e-signature once legal confirms language. Expect a DocuSign link early next week.

One note: we cannot accept the clause that creates an indefinite migration liability. That was the only material blocker. If Acme can accept the above, we are ready to execute.

I'll follow up with the DocuSign packet and a redline summary. Appreciate the urgency — we'll do our best to keep you on track for June.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
